documents.title: Students and AI (Library guide)
documents.summary: A short library guide telling students to read syllabi and ask each professor before using any AI tool, and warning that unasked use risks misconduct accusations. It quotes the Information Security Policy section barring institutional data from unauthorized generative AI, and points to Career Services guidance.
documents.stance_why: The guide sets no AI rule for coursework itself: "Every professor will have different expectations about AI-based tools," and students must "ask your professors before you use any AI-based tools," so the decision is delegated to instructors.

units.why: The sentence tells students to read syllabi and ask professors before using "any AI-based tools" in any course activity, so it is a student-facing rule that AI use needs prior clearance. Coded P10 (ask before using) rather than P04 because it addresses what the student must do; P04 is the separate statement that professors differ.
units.anchor: you ask your professors before you use any AI-based tools

units.why: "Every professor will have different expectations" is a statement that AI rules vary by instructor, which places the decision with each professor. Coded P04 because it hands the rule to individual instructors; it is not itself a rule, so modality is informs.
units.anchor: Every professor will have different expectations about AI-based tools.

units.why: "It is your responsibility to ask to use AI" puts the burden of seeking permission on the student, so AI use is not assumed allowed. Coded P10; it overlaps the first unit but is a distinct sentence stressing the burden of asking.
units.anchor: It is your responsibility to ask to use AI.
units.fit_note: Also frames asking as the student's responsibility, not only advice to ask when unsure.

units.why: "It your responsibility ensure that you are not committing any academic integrity violations" makes the student responsible for staying within integrity rules when using AI. Nearest type is P29 (students own what they submit), but the passage is about responsibility for compliance, not ownership of work.
units.anchor: It your responsibility ensure that you are not committing any academic integrity violations.
units.fit_note: Responsibility is for avoiding integrity violations, not for owning or explaining submitted work.

units.why: "you assume certain risks including serious accusations of misconduct" warns that unapproved AI use can lead to misconduct charges, so it treats unauthorized use as misconduct (P36). It is a warning rather than a stated penalty, so P37 does not fit.
units.anchor: you assume certain risks including serious accusations of misconduct
units.frag_start: If you choose to use AI tools

units.why: The warning that unapproved use risks "failure to meet the learning objectives of the class" gives a learning reason for asking first. Coded P41 because the stated concern is that AI use may undermine the learning the course is built to produce; P43 (false mastery) is not claimed.
units.anchor: failure to meet the learning objectives of the class
units.frag_start: If you choose to use AI tools
units.fit_note: States the risk to learning objectives without explaining how AI shortcuts practice.

units.why: "Institutional data must not be used with generative AI systems that are not operated or explicitly authorized" is a prohibition on entering Institute data into outside AI, quoted from Information Security Policy 4.2.3. Coded P50 (protect data, prefer vetted tools) as it concerns data protection and authorized tools; it binds all users, so actor is all.
units.anchor: Institutional data must not be used with generative AI systems that are not operated

units.why: "Examples include public or commercial AI platforms accessed via web browsers or APIs" defines which outside systems the data rule covers. Coded P61 because it sets the scope of the covered tools.
units.anchor: public or commercial AI platforms accessed via web browsers or APIs

units.why: "prohibited unless the data is fully anonymized, and the use case has been reviewed and approved by the Information Security Team" sets a narrow exception with an approval step. Coded P50 as a data-protection condition; the review of the use case by a security team is a fit gap.
units.anchor: prohibited unless the data is fully anonymized, and the use case has been reviewed
units.fit_note: Adds a security-team approval requirement for exceptions, beyond protecting data and preferring vetted tools.

units.why: "Such use constitutes data misuse ... violating Institute policy and applicable regulations" classes unauthorized data use as a policy and legal violation. Coded P77 (comply with law and university policy) rather than P36, which concerns academic misconduct.
units.anchor: Such use constitutes data misuse and may result in unauthorized disclosure, violating Institute policy

units.why: The guide points students to Career Services' "general tips ... on responsible and ethical uses of AI tools for career development" and to their Career Advisor. Coded P72 (human help alongside AI) because it directs students to staff; the guidance is about AI use in careers, which P72 does not name.
units.anchor: Consult with your Rose-Hulman Career Advisor for additional details.
units.fit_note: Refers to guidance on responsible AI use for career development, not general help with coursework.

notes: Only one included document; no institute-level, school, or computing policy found. Course syllabi deferred in collect file.
